events.title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
events.description: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, and his wife Sophie were shot in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb nationalist affiliated with the Young Bosnia movement.
events.significance: The assassination triggered the July Crisis, leading Austria-Hungary to declare war on Serbia and setting off a chain of alliances that escalated into World War I.

events.title: Treaty of Versailles Signed
events.description: Germany and the Allied Powers signed the Treaty of Versailles in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, exactly five years after the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.
events.significance: The treaty formally ended World War I, imposed territorial losses, military restrictions, and reparations on Germany, and created the League of Nations. Its harsh terms are often cited as a factor in the rise of Nazism and World War II.

events.title: Coronation of Queen Victoria
events.description: Victoria was crowned Queen of the United Kingdom at Westminster Abbey, a year after she ascended the throne at age 18 following the death of her uncle William IV.
events.significance: Her reign of over 63 years, the Victorian era, saw the expansion of the British Empire, the Industrial Revolution, and major social and cultural change.

events.title: Battle of Sullivan's Island
events.description: American defenders at a palmetto-log fort in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, under Colonel William Moultrie repelled a British naval attack led by Admiral Peter Parker.
events.significance: The victory delayed British operations in the South for years and boosted American morale just days before the Declaration of Independence was adopted.

events.title: Birth of Henry VIII
events.description: Henry VIII, future King of England, was born at Greenwich Palace, the second son of Henry VII and Elizabeth of York.
events.significance: Henry VIII broke with the Roman Catholic Church, established the Church of England, and reshaped English religion, government, and the monarchy during his reign.
